name: Asana
one_liner: Work management platform for tasks, projects, and workspaces, with a REST API.
auth_notes: PATs and service account tokens sent as Bearer; OAuth2 apps registered in developer console with permission scopes.
access_notes: PATs generated in developer console; API rate limits published for both Free and Paid domains, so API works on free plans. Service accounts are Enterprise-only.

buildability.rationale: Self-serve PATs and OAuth with scopes; free-domain rate limits imply free API access; HMAC-signed webhooks; official MCP.

auth.quote: You can generate a personal access token from the Asana developer console.
Asana uses OAuth 2.0 for secure user authorization.

access.quote: Limits are based on minute-long windows and differ depending on whether the domain is free or paid

api_surface.quote: Webhooks allow an application to be notified of changes in Asana.
Limits are allocated per authorization token. Different tokens have independent limits.

mcp.quote: Asana offers a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, accessible via app integration

identity.quote: Much like an API key, generating a PAT allows you to access

disputes.why: Asana developer docs describe an Asana-offered MCP server.
Rate limit table includes Free domains, so API is available on free plan.
Free tier has API access; only service accounts are Enterprise-only.
